findings.issue: The sampler now writes runout cards inline with the same loop as Table.setRunout, which only the exact path still uses. Two copies of the slot arithmetic (7 - need + index) must stay in sync.
findings.evidence: setRunout at line 188 computes slot = 7 - this.need + index. The sampler uses firstRunout = 7 - need and loops slot from firstRunout to 6.
findings.fix: Optional: leave as is for the hot loop, or have the sampler call table.setRunout(slot - firstRunout, card) if profiling shows no cost.

summary: The judge-fix commit gives the same outputs and weakens no check. Typed arrays: the Float64Array tallies hold the same doubles as the old number[] tallies, and Int32Array ranks are safe because evaluate returns 1..7462. The sampler writes hole cards into hands before a trial is accepted, but score() runs only after every opponent slot has been written in that trial, so a rejected trial's leftover writes are always overwritten. The marked[] layout and the RNG call order are unchanged. The runout loop covers the same slots as setRunout. A direct old-vs-new comparison found identical output on sampled and exact paths, and the PRNG streams match. No test files changed, the locked test hash matches, and all advice and seeded-random tests pass. The global testTimeout is the user-approved Q-5 change. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings; two NITs.
